audit.whatIsWrong: Level-chart stages carried a closing verdict that contradicted the stage owner (for example a stage marked Cho'Gath ending "Camille is favoured here").
audit.why: The full-layer phase text was templated; the tail sentence was never reconciled with phases[].side, so the written verdict and the chart disagreed on the same page.
audit.corrected: Each phase why now closes with the verdict that matches its own side field, so early / mid / side-lane ownership reads consistently.

audit.why: Spike stages line up with the real kits: Camille at 2 (Hookshot, 16s at rank 1), 6 (The Hextech Ultimatum, 140s at rank 1) and her Sheen item; Cho'Gath at Feast (80/70/60).

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 stage told you to "use the cast's brief untargetable frame" on The Hextech Ultimatum to dodge Cho'Gath's key spell.
audit.why: Riot's own description of The Hextech Ultimatum is "Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area" — there is no untargetable window. The kit file's untargetable/channel flags on R are tooltip-parse misfires and contradict the description.
audit.corrected: The stage now says the dash grants no immunity and keys R to being spent after the enemy spell rather than into it.

edits.before: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. Use the cast's brief untargetable frame to dodge Cho'Gath's Rupture or burst, then focus the trapped target. This is a clean skill phase.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates a target in a 1v1 they cannot leave. The dash grants no immunity, so spend R once Cho'Gath's Rupture is gone, not into it, then focus the trapped target. This is a clean skill phase.

edits.before: The clock is Cho'Gath's friend, not yours. Once he has stacked Feast and a giant HP pool, his R is a point-and-click true-damage percent execute that ignores your Adaptive Defense shield and your W heal entirely, and your Tactical Sweep's max-HP damage stops keeping pace with the raw health he builds. Win this lane outright in the early-to-mid window and use R to pick him in skirmishes; if the game drags to his 2+ item spike, stop dueling him head-on and let your team collapse on the giant rather than eat his Feast.
edits.after: The clock is Cho'Gath's friend, not yours. Once he has stacked Feast and a giant HP pool, his R is a point-and-click true-damage percent execute that ignores your Adaptive Defenses shield and your W heal entirely, and your Tactical Sweep's max-HP damage stops keeping pace with the raw health he builds. Win this lane outright in the early-to-mid window and use R to pick him in skirmishes; if the game drags to his 2+ item spike, stop dueling him head-on and let your team collapse on the giant rather than eat his Feast.

edits.before: Stacked Feast HP and his point-and-click Feast execute flip the duel — once he has a giant health pool your W%-damage falls behind and his true-damage R ignores both your Adaptive Defense shield and W heal.
edits.after: Stacked Feast HP and his point-and-click Feast execute flip the duel — once he has a giant health pool your W%-damage falls behind and his true-damage R ignores both your Adaptive Defenses shield and W heal.

notes: Camille kit file flags R as channel/interruptible and untargetable; both contradict Riot's own description (a dash plus an anchoring zone) and were treated as tooltip-parse misfires, per the kit README. Packet win rate 53.21% over 265 games.
